defects.justification: Anything that is not a directory or symlink is treated as a regular file; a FIFO or device under a backed-up directory makes File.open/IO.copy_stream block forever, hanging the run while holding the mutex, so every later scheduled run blocks too.

Dir.glob on a configured directory that does not exist (or is unreadable) returns [], so the run uploads an archive missing that directory and reports status 'ok'; misconfigured or unmounted sources fail silently.

The tar header is written with file.size taken before copying; a file that grows during archiving raises and fails the whole backup, and one that shrinks leaves a mis-sized entry, so live log/database files break runs.
The archive is uploaded with a single put_object, which S3 limits to 5 GB; larger backups always fail. Multipart upload (upload_file) is needed.
retention_days is never validated; with 0 or a negative value the cutoff is now or in the future, so prune deletes the archive that was just uploaded, along with every other backup.
The status server spawns an unbounded thread per connection and calls client.gets with no timeout or length limit, so idle or slow clients can pile up threads and memory.
The scheduling path, --once flag and exit code in main are never tested, and neither are retention edge cases; the tests cover only Runner/Archiver/StatusServer.
